title: Sensitive intranuclear flow cytometric quantification of IRF4 protein in multiple myeloma and normal human hematopoietic cells
protocol: Wash cells in 2-3 mL of STM.
Prepare a single-stained compensation control sample for each fluorophore.
Create a Fluorescence minus one (FMO) antibody-deleted sample for each fluorophore.
Start with approximately 2–4 million cells resuspended in 2 mL of total STM.
Divide the cell suspension among the control wells.
Mix cells well by pipetting.
Aliquot 1 × 10^5 to 2.5 × 10^5 total cells per control well.
Use a volume of 100 μL per well for aliquots.
Alternatively, use compensation beads as single-color compensation controls.
Add one drop of compensation beads for each single stain control.
Add corresponding antibody to each compensation bead control.
Dispense cells for control samples into the appropriate number of wells.
Place control samples in columns 1 and 2 of a 96-well deep-well round (U)-bottom plate.
Centrifuge the plate for 5 min, 300 × g at 4°C.
Visually verify the presence of a cell pellet in the bottom of each well after centrifugation.

Discard the supernatant by holding the plate firmly and rapidly (but carefully) dump off the supernatant while using a single quick plunging motion to discard the waste over a bucket containing 10% bleach.
When the plate is turned back over, ensure a small residual volume of buffer remains in each well.
Use an aspirating pipette to remove the supernatant individually from each FACS tube.
Avoid touching the cell pellet while aspirating.
Gently vortex the plate with the lid on to loosen cell pellets into residual wash buffer.
Verify visually the presence of cell pellets in the bottom of the plate after centrifugation.
Rapidly discard the supernatant after visual verification.
Gently vortex the plate to loosen the cell pellets.
Add 300 μL of PBS to each well using a multichannel pipettor.
Pipette up and down to resuspend and wash the cells in each well.
Centrifuge the plate for 5 min at 300 × g at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant from the wells.
Gently vortex the plate to dislodge cell pellets.
Dilute Near-IR live/dead dye 1:1000 in PBS, preparing 100 μL per sample plus an excess of 10%.
Add diluted Near-IR dye to all appropriate samples, excluding unstained well, FMO Near-IR well, and single-stain wells for Near-IR except for the Near-IR single-stain.
Pipette up and down 2–3 times to thoroughly resuspend cells in dye.
Incubate plate(s) in the dark for 30 min at 20°C–25°C.
Add 300 μL of STM to each well after incubation.
Centrifuge plate for 5 min at 300 × g at 4°C.
Discard supernatant from the wells post-centrifugation.
Gently vortex the plate to dislodge cell pellets.
Ensure cells are washed with PBS before staining with Near-IR live/dead stain, as FBS can interfere with dye activity.
Dilute Human FcR block 1:25 in STM, making enough for 30 μL per sample plus an excess of at least 10%.
Add 30 μl of block solution to each sample.
Incubate plate(s) for 20 min in the dark at 4°C.
Prepare a 2× concentrated master mix of surface-stain antibodies, diluting them appropriately in STM.
Make enough volume to add 30 μL to each experimental sample plus an excess of at least 10%.
Add 30 μl of surface-stain antibody master mix to experimental samples receiving the full stain.
Pipette up and down 2–3 times to thoroughly resuspend cells in experimental samples.
Do not remove blocking solution before adding staining mix.
Do not add cell surface antibody master mix to single-stain and FMO wells.
Do not add IRF4 antibody into the cell surface antibody master mix or to any single-stain or FMO controls at this stage.
Add antibodies individually at the appropriate dilutions along with STM for single-stain and FMO controls.
Ensure each well reaches a total volume of 60 μL.
Incubate plate(s) for 45 min in the dark at 4°C.
Add 300 μL of STM to each well and centrifuge for 5 min, 300 × g at 4°C.
Discard supernatant and gently vortex plate to dislodge pellet.
Repeat step for a total of two washes.
Discard supernatant after the last wash.
Gently vortex the plate to dissociate cell pellets.
Add 200 μL of 1× True-Nuclear fixative solution to each well.
Gently pipette up and down to ensure all cells are resuspended.
Incubate at 20°C–25°C in the dark for 50 min (no longer than 60 min).
Do not incubate samples in True-Nuclear fixative solution for longer than 60 minutes.
Store samples in a fixative-free buffer if the protocol is paused for 12–18 hours.
Centrifuge plate at 300 × g for 5 minutes at 20°C–25°C after fixation.
Discard supernatant and gently vortex the plate to dislodge cell pellets.
Proceed immediately to Permeabilization and Intranuclear Staining Procedure or store cells in STM or CytoLast buffer at 4°C for 12–18 hours if pausing.
Wrap sides of plate tightly with parafilm to prevent evaporation when storing.
Cover plate in foil to protect from light during storage.
Centrifuge plate at 300 × g for 5 minutes at 20°C–25°C after a 12–18-hour pause.
Discard supernatant and gently vortex the plate to dislodge pellets before permeabilization.
Permeabilize cell and nuclear membranes using True-Nuclear Perm Buffer.
Add 300 μL of 1× True-Nuclear Perm Buffer to each well.
Centrifuge plate at 300 × g for 5 min at 20°C–25°C.
Discard supernatant and gently vortex the plate to dislodge cell pellets.
Repeat permeabilization steps with Perm Buffer for a total of two washes.
Dilute IRF4 antibody in True-Nuclear Perm Buffer (1:100).
Prepare enough diluted antibody volume for 100 μL per sample plus an excess of at least 10%.
Store diluted antibody on ice, protected from light, until use.
Add diluted IRF4 antibody to all experimental samples receiving the full stain (100 μL per sample).
Also add diluted IRF4 antibody to the IRF4 single-stain sample and all FMO samples, except IRF4 FMO.
Add 100 μL of Perm Buffer alone to all other control samples.
Incubate in the dark at 20°C–25°C for 45 min.
Add 300 μL of 1× True-Nuclear Perm Buffer to each well.
Centrifuge plate at 300 × g for 5 min at 20°C–25°C.
Discard supernatant and gently vortex plate to dislodge pellet.
Repeat steps of adding Perm Buffer and centrifuging once more for a total of two washes in Perm Buffer.
Resuspend cells in 200–400 μL of STM.
Acquire samples on a flow cytometer equipped with the appropriate laser configuration for the fluorophores utilized.
Process all samples through a flow cytometer.
Ensure the flow cytometer includes 405 nm Violet, 488 nm Blue, 561 nm Yellow Green, and 633 nm Red lasers.
Initiate and prime the flow cytometer for acquisition.
Use the unstained control sample to set forward scatter and side scatter voltages.
Use single-stained controls to set voltages of other fluorophore channels and collect data for compensation.
Collect data using FMO samples for negative population gating.
Collect data from all control and experimental samples after setting voltages appropriately.
Ensure a minimum of 20,000–50,000 cells per experimental sample is collected (10,000 cells for each compensation control and FMO).
Export the collected data in FCS 3.0 format.
Filter noticeably clumpy or likely dead cell-rich samples through a cell strainer with a 35 μm mesh before acquisition if necessary.
Analyze the exported data using FlowJo software.
